notImplementedOnPlatform.windows: sessions compile but the platform session/TUN path is T6; no Windows run has been recorded

platform.note: Every runtime result here comes from macOS arm64, including the UDP and private-CA cases. A platform difference must be reproduced against the same-platform Mihomo; nothing is claimed for a platform that was not run.

statusVocabulary.implemented: the Rust kernel performs the behaviour and a loopback or pinned-Mihomo test observes it
statusVocabulary.partial: part of the upstream shape works; the missing options are named and rejected explicitly
statusVocabulary.unimplemented: the Rust kernel rejects the entry/field instead of ignoring it

optionPolicy: proxies.rs accepts only the keys its parser read and honoured, plus values Mihomo accepts and ignores: disabled booleans (`udp: false`, `disable-reuse: false`, `packet-addr: false`, `xudp: false`, `v2ray-http-upgrade-fast-open: false`), empty blocks (`grpc-opts: {}`, `ech-opts: {enable: false}`, `smux: {enabled: false}`, `ss-opts: {}`, `shadow-tls-opts: {}`, `restls-opts: {}`, `plugin-opts: {}`) and TLS-only options with TLS off (`skip-cert-verify`, `sni`, `alpn`, `fingerprint`, `certificate`, `private-key`, `name-cert-verify`, `client-fingerprint`, `ech-opts`, `reality-opts`). `reality-opts` and `jls-opts` require fields even when empty (Mihomo's `-t` rejects them), so their empty form fails here too. Every behaviour-changing form fails with the key named. tool/kernel-compat/option-probe.mjs compares the no-op and enabled forms against the pinned Mihomo `-t` and writes evidence/option-matrix.txt. A `udp: true` proxy with `dialer-proxy` must name exactly one socks5 hop; other chains fail at load time (validate_udp_chains). `reality-opts`, `shadow-tls-opts`, `restls-opts` and `jls-opts` require `tls: true` (Mihomo rejects them without TLS), so with TLS off a non-empty block fails; with TLS on, a non-empty block fails as not implemented. Keys the pinned type does not declare at all (`smux`, `ss-opts` on vless, `udp` on http, any unknown name) are ignored exactly as Mihomo ignores them.

port.reason: recorded only; the mixed listener is the only bound port

socks-port.reason: legacy alias for mixed-port with a warning

proxies.reason: twelve protocol types with their implemented transports, options and UDP associations (ss/trojan); every other type or option is rejected by name

tls.reason: custom-cert/certificate anchors are built into the kernel instance and used by every TLS dial; skip-cert-verify is the explicit override

socks5.udp: not implemented: `udp: true` is rejected (no SOCKS5 UDP relay to the server); `udp: false` loads

http.udp: not applicable: Mihomo's HTTP outbound has no UDP option, so any `udp` key is rejected as a non-Mihomo option

ss.udp: implemented: AEAD-2017 datagrams (`salt || sealed(addr || payload)`), replies decrypted with the server's salt; with `dialer-proxy` the datagrams travel through exactly one socks5 hop's UDP relay (any other chain fails at load time)

trojan.udp: implemented: command 3 over TLS with `addr|length|CRLF|payload` frames; the server connection is established through the `dialer-proxy` chain exactly like TCP (one socks5 hop)

vless.udp: not implemented: `udp: true` is rejected (needs packet-addr/XUDP); `udp: false` loads

anytls.udp: not implemented: `udp: true` is rejected (needs UoT); `udp: false` loads
anytls.notes: shadow-tls-opts/restls-opts/jls-opts are declared by the pinned anytls type and applied (they add a security mode to the TLS config), so a non-empty block is a registered rejection; the same keys on socks5/http/ss are not declared there and are ignored.

vmess.udp: not implemented: `udp: true` is rejected (no VMess UDP command); `udp: false` loads

snell.udp: not implemented: `udp: true` is rejected (no Snell UDP command); `udp: false` loads

trusttunnel.udp: not implemented: `udp: true` is rejected (`_udp2` multiplex); `udp: false` loads

gost-relay.reason: TCP relay with optional TLS, username/password authentication, `forward`, the UDP association and the version-1 smux session. The controlled peer is the loopback relay v2 server in tests/protocols.rs, written from transport/gost/relay.go; the smux frame layout is pinned by a unit test. The controlled peer is also driven by the pinned `gost.NewRelayDialer` (`tool/kernel-compat/peers/gost-relay-harness`, with mux and UDP), so the UDP association and the smux session are not only checked against our own client.
options: udp (one association bound to one target; `length(u16 BE) || payload` frames)
mux (smux DefaultConfig version 1, keep-alive disabled, one stream per dial)
gost-relay.udp: implemented: `udp: true` opens the pinned association (command 0x81, network feature 1, address feature = the bound target); a server that refuses it produces no reply and no DIRECT fallback

ssh.reason: password and inline-PEM public-key authentication, host-key pinning and one direct-tcpip channel per dial; a private-key file path is rejected by name and each dial opens its own SSH client (Mihomo reuses one client per proxy).
ssh.udp: not applicable: Mihomo's SSH outbound reports UDP false; any `udp` key is rejected as a non-Mihomo option

ssr.reason: every pinned stream cipher plus every protocol plugin (origin, auth_sha1_v4, auth_aes128_md5, auth_aes128_sha1, auth_chain_a, auth_chain_b), every obfs plugin (plain, http_simple, http_post, random_head, tls1.2_ticket_auth, tls1.2_ticket_fastauth) and the UDP association. The wire format is checked against an independent Go peer built from the pinned packages (`tool/kernel-compat/peers/ssr-plugins`), which also runs the pinned client packages against itself. random_head locates the peer head by scanning the CRC from the longest candidate: the pinned CRC check is not unique for every length (crc32(head[:n-1]) can match the four bytes at n-1), and an ascending scan occasionally took the head one byte short and misaligned the cipher stream.
options: cipher (rc4-md5, aes-128/192/256-cfb, aes-128/192/256-ctr, chacha20, chacha20-ietf, xchacha20, none)
protocol-param (user id and key; the plugin's own parsing)
udp (the pinned cipher.PacketConn + protocol.PacketConn association; no obfs layer, as in the pinned outbound)
ssr.udp: implemented: `udp: true` opens the pinned association (IV || cipher(protocol packet), SOCKS5 address inside, no obfs). Every protocol is verified against the Go peer and a wrong password is rejected. Limit inherited from the pinned client: `auth_aes128_*` datagrams are sealed with the derived user key but opened with the cipher key, so a `protocol-param` breaks the UDP path in both directions; the UDP tests therefore use no protocol-param (TCP with `protocol-param` is covered).

mieru.reason: TCP single sessions are implemented; the UDP transport, `udp: true` (UDP associate), the multiplexing levels and `traffic-pattern` are rejected at load with the reason recorded (T13 scope)
mieru.udp: not implemented: `udp: true` (the UDP-associate wrapper) is rejected; TCP sessions only
notes: the mieru module is GPL-3.0, so the client is an independent implementation of docs/protocol.md (PBKDF2-SHA256 time salt, XChaCha20-Poly1305 implicit nonce with the user hint, 32-byte metadata, session/data segments, one TCP session per underlay); no mieru code is vendored or linked
handshake-mode values load: HANDSHAKE_NO_WAIT only defers the same handshake, and the kernel dials eagerly
port-range picks a random member per dial (up to four tries) because any port in the range is a valid server endpoint

masque.reason: T18 implements both shapes the pinned adapter serves. (1) RFC 9484 CONNECT-IP over HTTP/3 for the Cloudflare WARP configuration: the base64 SEC1 P-256 client key generates the pinned adapter's self-signed client certificate, `public-key` (a DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo) pins the endpoint certificate, and the request is `:method CONNECT`, `:protocol cf-connect-ip`, `:scheme https`, `:authority`/`:path` from `uri` (default https://cloudflareaccess.com) with `capsule-protocol: ?1`. The client advertises ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT (0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255 and ::-all-ones, protocol 0, as the pinned adapter does), reads ADDRESS_ASSIGN/ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT, and carries whole IPv4/IPv6 packets as HTTP Datagrams (QUIC DATAGRAM frames with quarter stream ID + Context ID 0; inbound DATAGRAM capsules are accepted too). `ip`/`ipv6` are the tunnel's local addresses, `mtu` bounds one packet, `ip-stack.mode auto|mips` selects the stack (the in-tree UDP-only one; gVisor is the pinned build-tagged dependency and is rejected), and `remote-dns-resolve`+`dns` send A/AAAA queries through the tunnel. The kernel's minimal IP stack (src/outbound/ipstack.rs) terminates UDP only: a TCP dial is refused by name because serving TCP needs a TCP state machine (the pinned adapter uses mipstack/gVisor). (2) The RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP subset from T14 still serves a plain server with `udp: true`. One QUIC connection per UDP association (no pooling), QUIC datagrams rather than capsule-carried datagrams for sending, no server push/WebTransport/0-RTT; `network: h2|h3-l4proxy`, the QUIC congestion-controller options and `dialer-proxy` are named.
masque.udp: implemented in both shapes. CONNECT-IP: one UDP flow (local source port) per destination, at most 32 flows per association (least-recently-used eviction beyond that), packets built with IPv4 header/UDP checksums or the mandatory IPv6 UDP checksum, `mtu` (pinned default 1280) bounding one datagram, replies matched by (local address, local port, remote address); tunnel DNS is a UDP A/AAAA query to the configured name servers. CONNECT-UDP: one request stream per destination, DATAGRAM capsules with context ID 0, closed flows reclaimed before the cap is enforced.
notImplemented: TCP over masque (CONNECT-IP carries IP packets; serving TCP needs a TCP state machine the kernel does not have)
ip-stack.mode: gvisor (the pinned build-tagged gVisor dependency)
remote-dns-resolve with DNS over TCP/DoT/DoH or `#param` name servers
ADDRESS_REQUEST from the peer (no address-assignment policy)
IPv6 extension headers and IPv4 fragments (reported and dropped, not reassembled)
ICMP error generation (a datagram too large for the QUIC datagram limit is an error, not a synthesised ICMP)
DATA frames larger than 2 KiB on the CONNECT-IP request stream are refused (local bound)
more than 32 concurrent destinations/flows per association (local bound)
notes: the client is written from RFC 9484, 9298, 9297, 9220 and 9114 plus the pinned adapter's recorded configuration shape; no pinned Go code (metacubex/connect-ip-go, mipstack, gVisor, quic-go, metacubex/http) is vendored, linked or copied. DER/base64/calendar helpers in src/outbound/warp.rs and the IP/UDP codec in src/outbound/ipstack.rs are original code; the signature comes from `ring`, already the TLS provider

the controlled CONNECT-IP peer in tests/quic_peers.rs is an independent quinn HTTP/3 server with its own IP/UDP codec; it requires the WARP client certificate (recording the SubjectPublicKeyInfo), advertises extended CONNECT plus SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM 0x33 and draft-00 0x276, sends ADDRESS_ASSIGN and echoes tunnelled packets; a second peer mode omits datagram settings and a third sends ADDRESS_REQUEST
no pinned-binary masque interop is claimed: the pinned adapter has no listener and a WARP registration endpoint is not reachable offline

T7 memory: the CONNECT-IP association uses the T10 quinn profile (stream receive window 512 KiB, connection receive 2 MiB, send 2 MiB) plus 64 KiB datagram receive/send buffers, one request stream with a 2 KiB DATA-frame and 4 KiB capsule bound, 4 queued inbound packets, 32 flows and at most 8 held datagrams during a DNS lookup; the per-association worst case (~5.3 MB decimal) is in t18-feasibility.json and T7 must cap concurrent associations
`name-cert-verify` is a pinned placeholder that verifies nothing, so it is accepted as a no-op; `skip-cert-verify` drops the endpoint-key pin exactly like the pinned option
IPv4 options, IPv4 fragments, IPv6 extension headers, TCP and ICMP are refused/dropped with a log line; nothing is silently forwarded

`ip-stack.congestion-controller` values (cubic/reno/bbr/bbr3) are validated and accepted as a no-op: they select the TCP congestion controller of the userspace stack, and TCP is not terminated (the same gap as TCP over masque)

the shipped CLI process is covered: cli.rs::process_loads_t18_masque_connect_ip (WARP shape loads, TCP refused, process stays up) and family_cli.rs::cli_process_tunnels_udp_through_masque_connect_ip (SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE through a CONNECT-IP peer)
the client does not send ADDRESS_REQUEST (the pinned adapter uses the configured ip/ipv6 prefixes and the server's ADDRESS_ASSIGN); a peer ADDRESS_REQUEST fails the association by name

sudoku.reason: TCP sessions with the legacy HTTP mask, the pure and packed downlink codecs, table rotation, all three record AEAD methods, the session mux (`multiplex: on`) and `dialer-proxy` (the exit's server connection is carried by a socks5 hop chain, repaired in T17-A3) are translated from the pinned GPL-3.0 `transport/sudoku` (T17); the HTTP tunnel modes (`stream`/`poll`/`auto`/`ws`) and the UoT association are rejected at load with the reason recorded
sudoku.license: GPL-3.0-derived translation of Mihomo `transport/sudoku` v1.19.34 (commit 0455d0d28c4526937380505153e65a843d8612e8); the kernel workspace is GPL-3.0-only, any distribution of the combined work must follow GPL-3.0 (source availability etc.), see native-kernel/COPYING.GPL-3.0 and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
sudoku.udp: not implemented: `udp: true` (the UoT association, `KIPTypeStartUoT` + `transport/sudoku/uot.go`) is rejected at load; the kernel's UDP association selection for sudoku is a T9 decision
notes: the module files carry `SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only` and the upstream version/commit; `src/keys.rs` (`sudoku_seed`) and `src/proxies.rs` (`SudokuOutbound`, `parse_sudoku`) are mixed files with the same header on the derived item and the scope stated in their module docs; distribution must follow GPL-3.0 (native-kernel/COPYING.GPL-3.0)

`dialer-proxy`: the dispatch builds the exit's server connection through the hop chain (`src/outbound/mod.rs::connect_via_hops`) and runs the sudoku handshake over it; the exit is never dropped, and exits whose protocol cannot run over a stream fail with a chain error instead of letting a hop dial the target. The mux session cache key includes the hop chain and is cleared when the engine stops

multiplex is the translated client side of `transport/sudoku/multiplex/session.go` (frames open/data/close/reset/ping/pong, one shared session per configuration, recreated after failure); frames are queued whole so streams do not interleave
the HTTP tunnel modes are a mihomo extension (`transport/sudoku/obfs/httpmask/tunnel_*`, ~1.8k lines) and stay rejected by name; the legacy header mask is implemented
tables are built once per configuration (288-grid shuffle, 1820 puzzle candidates per byte) and cached in-process
`multiplex: auto` behaves like `off`: the pinned mode only reuses an HTTP tunnel connection, and the HTTP tunnel layer is rejected
evidence: tests/mihomo_peers.rs (12 sudoku cases: entropy/ascii/directional/custom/rotation tables, packed downlink, three AEAD methods, with/without the HTTP mask, private/public key material, a dialer-proxy chain through a recording SOCKS5 hop, wrong key, mismatched table type)

tuic.reason: TUIC v5 over QUIC: uuid/password authentication (TLS exporter token), one TCP stream per session, and `request-timeout` bounding the auth/Connect stream operations; the legacy v4 token (BLAKE3 TKN) is rejected, the UDP relay modes are not wired into the engine, and one QUIC connection is created per dial instead of the pinned pool.
tuic.udp: not implemented: the engine's UDP association has no TUIC datagram/uni-stream relay; UDP traffic routed to TUIC is dropped and logged

hysteria.reason: Hysteria v1 over QUIC: TCP with the binary control hello (auth/auth-str, up/down) and one stream per session; port hopping, the XPlus obfuscator, the faketcp/wechat transports and UDP datagrams are rejected by name.
hysteria.udp: not implemented: the engine has no Hysteria UDP session relay; `udp` traffic routed to Hysteria is dropped and logged

hysteria2.reason: Hysteria2 over QUIC: HTTP/3 authentication (`/auth`, status 233) and one TCP stream per session with the 0x401 request frame; `down` is sent as Hysteria-CC-RX. Port hopping, Salamander/Gecko obfuscation, realm, UDP and `up` (the Brutal TX-rate cap) are rejected by name.
hysteria2.udp: not implemented: the engine has no Hysteria2 UDP session relay; `udp` traffic routed to Hysteria2 is dropped and logged

shadowquic.reason: TCP and UDP (QUIC datagrams and `udp-over-stream`) are implemented against the pinned listener with an independent JLS random seal and a protocol-level transport; provenance is in tool/kernel-compat/evidence/t15-cleanroom.md; `zero-rtt`, QUIC `v2` and the private Brutal congestion options are rejected by name because quinn has no Brutal controller/JLS 0-RTT ticket
shadowquic.notes: recv-window defaults follow the kernel T7 budget (512 KiB stream / 2 MiB connection) rather than the pinned 1.57 MiB / 6.4 MiB initial windows; those are local flow-control choices, not wire fields. max-datagram-frame-size sizes the datagram buffers; the usable datagram payload is also path-MTU-bound, so larger UDP packets use udp-over-stream.
shadowquic.license: JLS vectors: BSD-3-Clause (Copyright 2009 The Go Authors), full text in native-kernel/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. ShadowQUIC transport: no GPL-3.0 source copied; provenance and the residual source-consultation caveat are recorded in tool/kernel-compat/evidence/t15-cleanroom.md.

wireguard.reason: The WireGuard transport (Noise IK, cookie reply, pre-shared key, transport keys, padding, replay window, initiator rekey, keepalive) is implemented in src/outbound/wireguard.rs and verified against the locked metacubex/wireguard-go device; TCP/UDP through the tunnel needs the userspace IP stack and TUN device owned by T6/T7, so dial() refuses with that gap named. AmneziaWG, an explicit ip-stack mode, the stack resolver and endpoint refresh are rejected by name.
wireguard.notes: Both peer forms load: `peers:` and the embedded top-level server/port/public-key form. `allowed-ips` defaults to 0.0.0.0/0 and/or ::/0 from ip/ipv6 in the single-peer form; `mtu` defaults to 1408. The transport is initiator-only for rekeys (it rekeys before the responder's 120 s window); answering a server-initiated handshake is not implemented.
wireguard.license: No wireguard/boringtun crate; no Go source vendored, linked, or translated. The locked MIT wireguard-go device is a test peer only. The pinned adapter/outbound/wireguard.go (GPL-3.0) was read for option names/defaults; this is source consultation, not a certified clean-room. Audit and limits: tool/kernel-compat/evidence/t16-provenance.md.

tailscale.reason: The control-base Noise IK transport, the HTTP/2 /machine/map request and the DERP greeting/client-info/ping/packet frames are implemented in src/outbound/tailscale.rs and verified against a controlled peer built from the locked BSD-3-Clause tailscale module. Node registration is not implemented, so hostname/auth-key/state-dir/ephemeral/accept-routes:true/exit-node/exit-node-allow-lan-access:true are rejected at load. TCP/UDP through the tunnel needs the T6/T7 userspace IP stack and TUN device, so dial() refuses with that gap named.
tailscale.notes: control-url is used by the protocol layer; the control server key is a library parameter. Registration-only options are explicit rejections, not silently accepted. Basic socket-shaping options and dialer-proxy are rejected with the T6/T7 boundary.
tailscale.license: No Tailscale source is copied or linked; the locked BSD-3-Clause module is a test peer only. See tool/kernel-compat/evidence/t19-mesh.md.

zerotier.reason: Identity generation/parsing (address proof of work), planet/moon parsing, VL1 packet armor (Salsa20/12 + Poly1305 and protocol-13 extended HELLO), HELLO/OK/WHOIS/ECHO and the VL2 frame payload are implemented in src/outbound/zerotier.rs and verified against a controlled peer built from the locked MPL-2.0 zerotier-go module. An explicit ip-stack, remote-dns-resolve/dns, remote trace and the TCP fallback transport (force/non-empty relay) are rejected with the T6/T7/T5 boundary. TCP/UDP through the network needs the T6/T7 userspace IP stack, and the controller membership exchange is T5, so dial() refuses with that gap named.
zerotier.notes: tcp-fallback-mode auto/disable with an empty relay is accepted because it asks for no transport; force or a non-empty relay is rejected. The controller membership/config verbs are T5.
zerotier.license: No ZeroTier source is copied or linked; the locked MPL-2.0 module is a test peer only. See tool/kernel-compat/evidence/t19-mesh.md.

easytier.reason: T19 rejected the whole type: the pinned core derives `network_secret_digest` inside its wasm artifact and that derivation is not reproducible from the offline source/crate cache. A placeholder digest is reset by the real core, so neither the cleartext host/discovery path nor `enable-encryption: true` is loaded as compatible. Device/TUN remains T6/T7.
easytier.notes: Rejected at configuration load with the digest gap named; no protocol object or peer is exposed as compatible.

openvpn.reason: The control channel (UDP/TCP framing, hard reset, reliable ACKs, TLS 1.2/1.3 client authentication, key-method 2) and the AEAD data channel are implemented in src/outbound/openvpn.rs and verified against OpenVPN 2.7.9; TCP/UDP through the tunnel needs the T6/T7 userspace IP stack and TUN device, so dial() refuses with that gap named. tls-auth/tls-crypt, compression and CBC data ciphers are rejected by name.
openvpn.notes: `ca` is an inline PEM and is required; the server chain is verified against it without a hostname check (matching the pinned client). `cert`/`key` are inline PEM and optional; without them the server may reject the TLS client (observed as a bounded handshake timeout). The data ciphers are AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM and CHACHA20-POLY1305; AES-192-GCM and CBC are not implemented.
openvpn.license: No OpenVPN crate; no OpenVPN/Mihomo source vendored, linked, or copied line-by-line. The GPL-2.0 OpenVPN binary is a test peer only. The pinned transport/openvpn (GPL-3.0) was read for functional wire facts; this is not a certified clean-room. Audit and limits: tool/kernel-compat/evidence/t16-provenance.md.

mixed.reason: one mixed port (HTTP CONNECT + SOCKS5 CONNECT + SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE) from `mixed-port`/`socks-port`; the top-level `listeners:` section is rejected until T5
notImplemented: UDP over the mixed port's HTTP side

socks.reason: SOCKS5 CONNECT and UDP ASSOCIATE are served on the mixed port; `listeners: type: socks` is rejected (T5)

http.reason: HTTP CONNECT (and 405 for other methods) on the mixed port; `listeners: type: http` is rejected (T5)

GEOSITE.reason: text database only; compiled MRS/protobuf is T5

familiesNotImplemented.note: T4 delivered 9 outbound types; T11 added gost-relay/ssh/ssr; T10 added tuic/hysteria/hysteria2 (QUIC); T13 added mieru (clean-room TCP) and T17 added sudoku as a GPL-3.0-derived translation (TCP, legacy HTTP mask, pure/packed, session mux); T14 added masque, T15 shadowquic, T16 the wireguard/openvpn transport adapters. T5 owns the built-in direct/dns/reject/rematch adapters.

direct.reason: built-in; DIRECT is already a rule action

dns.reason: built-in adapter that needs the DNS resolver

reject.reason: built-in; REJECT is already a rule action

easytier.reason: the pinned core's cleartext network_secret_digest derivation is not public/offline; both cleartext and encrypted forms are rejected by name. Device/TUN remains T6/T7.

unmappedNotes: Every proxy type outside the implemented ones is rejected at load time with its type named, never ignored; familiesNotImplemented records the task that implements it (T9 non-QUIC, T10 QUIC/device, T5 built-ins).
Every other listener type (tun, redir, tproxy, mixed with TLS, ...) is rejected through the top-level keys that would enable it.
Every other rule type is rejected with the rule text; the capability index keeps the full upstream list so T5 can record it.

T12 closed the SSR plugin layers (every pinned protocol/obfs plus the UDP association) and the gost-relay UDP association and smux session; the remaining SSR/gost-relay options are the transport knobs Mihomo accepts and ignores (ip-version/tfo/mptcp/interface-name/routing-mark) and gost-relay's certificate pinning knobs.

ignoredByPinnedVersion.note: Keys the pinned type does not declare (or declares only as a no-op in the given configuration) are accepted and ignored, exactly as Mihomo ignores them. They are not compatibility gaps.

ss: client-fingerprint (only read by a plugin, which is rejected)

global: any key no proxy type declares (a typo or a newer option)

quicProfile.tls: rustls 0.23, TLS 1.3 only, ALPN per family (h3 for TUIC/Hysteria2/masque/shadowquic, hysteria for Hysteria v1); shadowquic seals the ClientHello/ServerHello random with JLS and verifies the server random before certificate verification
quicProfile.offlineSource: local cargo registry cache; no h3/qpack/connect-ip/IP-stack/wireguard/mesh/OpenVPN crate is cached. JLS has no Rust crate: T15 implements the random seal in-tree and uses the locked jls-tls package only as a vector generator (tool/kernel-compat/peers/shadowquic-jls-vectors). quinn-proto and typenum became direct dependencies for the session wrapper and the 32-byte GCM nonce; both were already in the lockfile.
quicProfile.memory: one Endpoint + one Connection per dial (masque: per UDP association); transport windows capped to stream receive 512 KiB, connection receive 2 MiB, send 2 MiB, datagram buffers 64 KiB (quinn defaults: 1.25 MB / VarInt::MAX / 10 MB / ~1 MB). masque adds at most 32 request streams per association, each with a 2 x 65,535 B outbound queue and at most 131,102 B of pending capsule data; its per-association worst case (~19 MB decimal, including the QUIC windows) is recorded in t14-feasibility.json. shadowquic uses the same endpoint/connection profile plus one control stream and a 32-packet receive queue per UDP association; its `max-datagram-frame-size` (default 1400) sizes the datagram buffers. T7 must measure the whole iOS extension against the 40,000,000-byte budget; these tasks record the dependency and the caps, not a device measurement.
quicProfile.platform: macOS arm64 loopback and pinned-Mihomo runs; Linux/Android/iOS compile from the same code path; Windows compiles but no run is recorded
